title: The pro-étale site of a point
statement: The site $*_{\Proet}$ has as objects the profinite sets and as morphisms the continuous maps; a finite family $\{S_i\to S\}$ is a covering if $\coprod_iS_i\to S$ is surjective, and the topology is the one generated by these finite coverings (the coherent topology). A condensed ring is a sheaf of commutative rings on $*_{\Proet}$; equivalently, by Definition [pur713-def-ring-object], a commutative ring object of $\mathsf{Sh}(*_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$ with the sheafified tensor product. Source: governing reference, §3.1.

proof.text: Use the universe and skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. The point-site paragraph of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] gives exactly the category and topology used here: objects are profinite sets (compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces), arrows are continuous maps, and a covering sieve contains a finite jointly surjective family. Thus the site in this definition is that existing site. Here we restrict the term condensed ring to commutative rings, as the item explicitly stipulates; the cited node also allows noncommutative rings. The tensor and unit meant below are those of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], applied to this bounded profinite site with $\mathcal A=\Ab$: $F\otimes G=a(U\mapsto F(U)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G(U))$ and $\mathbf1=a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$, with $\underline{\mathbf Z}$ the constant presheaf.

source.place: Lecture IX, Definition 9.1 and Remark 9.2 (PDF pp. 84-85); tensor convention as in the item and det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure

proof.text: Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on this site. Apply [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf] with $C=*_{\Proet}$. It asserts that its underlying abelian presheaf is a sheaf and that its multiplication and unit extend uniquely to the sheafified tensor and sheafified integer presheaf. The same statement asserts commutativity when all section rings are commutative. Instantiate the abstract symmetric-monoidal-category definition of [pur713-def-ring-object] with $\mathscr C=\mathsf{Sh}(*_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$ and the tensor and unit of step 1. This gives precisely the multiplication, unit, associativity, two unit identities and commutativity required there. The current definition explicitly permits another named symmetric monoidal category; the category named here is the point-site category of step 1, whose tensor is over $\mathbf Z$ and whose unit is the sheafification of the constant integer presheaf. Thus its default notation $X_{\Proet}$ imposes no scheme hypothesis here. In this named category the equations are $\mu\circ(\mu\otimes\mathrm{id})=\mu\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes\mu)\circ\alpha$, $\mu\circ(e\otimes\mathrm{id})=\lambda$, $\mu\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes e)=\rho$, and $\mu\circ\beta=\mu$, with exactly the coherence maps specified in step 1. No topological-ring presentation of $\mathcal R$ is assumed.

source.place: Second sentence, forward direction of the equivalence; specialized existing sheaves-of-rings construction

proof.text: Conversely instantiate [pur713-def-ring-object] in the named category $\mathsf{Sh}(*_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$ with the tensor and unit of step 1, and let $(R,\mu,e)$ be a commutative ring object in it. Write $P=iR$ for its underlying abelian presheaf and $t_Q:Q\to iaQ$ for the sheafification map. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], $R\otimes R=a(P\otimes_pP)$ and $\mathbf1=a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$. Restrict the structure maps to presheaves: $m_p=i\mu\circ t_{P\otimes_pP}$ and $e_p=ie\circ t_{\underline{\mathbf Z}}$. At $S$ set $xy=(m_p)_S(x\otimes y)$ and $1_S=(e_p)_S(1)$. The tensor universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], for $\mathbf Z$-modules, makes the product additive in each variable. Explicitly, $x(y+z)=xy+xz$ and $(x+y)z=xz+yz$, since $(m_p)_S$ is a homomorphism from the integer tensor product; the additive abelian group is the given $R(S)$. Likewise $(e_p)_S(n)=n\cdot1_S$ because $(e_p)_S:\mathbf Z\to R(S)$ is additive. Thus the additive structure needed for a ring is already present before the monoid equations are evaluated. For associativity, put $b=t_{P\otimes_pP}:P\otimes_pP\to i(R\otimes R)$ and form $j_L=t_{i(R\otimes R)\otimes_pP}\circ(b\otimes_p\mathrm{id}_P)$ and $j_R=t_{P\otimes_pi(R\otimes R)}\circ(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes_pb)$. These have targets $i((R\otimes R)\otimes R)$ and $i(R\otimes(R\otimes R))$, respectively. The specified associator satisfies $i\alpha\circ j_L=j_R\circ\alpha_p$, where $\alpha_p$ is the objectwise associator. Naturality of $t$ gives $i(\mu\otimes\mathrm{id}_R)\circ j_L=b\circ(m_p\otimes_p\mathrm{id}_P)$ and $i(\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\mu)\circ j_R=b\circ(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes_pm_p)$. Precomposing the associativity equation with $j_L$ therefore gives $m_p\circ(m_p\otimes_p\mathrm{id}_P)=m_p\circ(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes_pm_p)\circ\alpha_p$, hence $(xy)z=x(yz)$ on $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$. Precomposing commutativity with $b$ gives $m_p\circ\beta_p=m_p$, hence $xy=yx$. For the left unit precompose with $t_{i\mathbf1\otimes_pP}\circ(t_{\underline{\mathbf Z}}\otimes_p\mathrm{id}_P)$; naturality of $t$ and the specified unitor give $m_p\circ(e_p\otimes_p\mathrm{id}_P)=\lambda_p$, hence $1_Sx=x$. For the right unit use $t_{P\otimes_pi\mathbf1}\circ(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes_pt_{\underline{\mathbf Z}})$ to get $m_p\circ(\mathrm{id}_P\otimes_pe_p)=\rho_p$, hence $x1_S=x$. All coherence maps here are exactly those in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]. Thus the existing abelian group $R(S)$, these products and these units form commutative rings. Naturality of $m_p,e_p$ says explicitly $R(u)(xy)=R(u)(x)R(u)(y)$ and $R(u)(1_S)=1_{S\prime}$ for every $u:S\prime\to S$. This is a presheaf of commutative rings. A matching family has exactly the same unique glued element as in the underlying abelian sheaf $R$, so it is a sheaf of commutative rings.

source.place: Second sentence, reverse direction, written out from the definitions; Stacks 00WH and 00YR (sites-proposition-sheafification-adjoint and sites-section-sheaves-algebraic-structures) and 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product) supply the cited universal properties

proof.text: These two constructions are inverse. Starting with a sheaf of rings, [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf] says its extended product and unit restrict to its original sectionwise maps, so step 3 recovers its ring operations. Starting with $(R,\mu,e)$, step 3 gives the restrictions $m_p,e_p$ of exactly those two maps. The sheaf-of-rings construction of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf] extends those restrictions, and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] says each such extension into the sheaf $R$ is unique. Hence the recovered maps are exactly $\mu,e$. This proves the asserted equivalence without identifying the sheafified tensor with an objectwise tensor of sheaves. On morphisms, a sheaf-of-rings morphism gives a ring-object morphism by [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf]. Conversely, for a ring-object morphism $f:R\to R\prime$, [pur713-def-ring-object] gives $f\circ\mu=\mu\prime\circ(f\otimes f)$ and $f\circ e=e\prime$. Precompose with $t_{P\otimes_pP}$ and $t_{\underline{\mathbf Z}}$: naturality gives $(if)\circ m_p=m_p\prime\circ(if\otimes_pif)$ and $(if)\circ e_p=e_p\prime$. Evaluating gives $f_S(xy)=f_S(x)f_S(y)$ and $f_S(1_S)=1_S\prime$, and $f_S$ is additive because $f$ is a morphism of abelian sheaves. These are all the unital ring-homomorphism conditions, so $f$ is a morphism of the recovered sheaves of commutative rings. Both constructions keep the underlying morphisms, hence preserve identities and composition and are inverse on morphisms as well.

source.place: Second sentence, verification that the two descriptions give the same objects; Stacks 00WH and 00YR, uniqueness in sheafification

Its statement matches main-20261015 pur713-def-point-site.md word for word and is true. Scholze's Lecture IX Def 9.1 and Rem 9.2 (pp. 84-85) give the same site: ProFin with finite jointly surjective covers, plus a size cutoff; the size cutoff matches def-weil-size-convention. Step 1 is elementary: the topology comes from sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, and the tensor a(F⊗_pG) and unit a(Z) are the Ab case of det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure, which explicitly lists the profinite site. Step 2 gets the forward direction from det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf, and det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf admits the profinite site. That node's ring object uses the same equations as pur713-def-ring-object in the named category Sh(*_Proet,Ab), so there is no change of coefficient category. Step 3 builds the converse, and I re-derived it: (a) i·alpha∘j_L = j_R∘alpha_p follows from the associator built from a(eta⊗id) and from naturality of t; (b) associativity, both unit laws and symmetry follow by precomposition; (c) bilinearity gives distributivity and e_p(n)=n·1; (d) the ring-sheaf gluing comes from the underlying abelian sheaf. Step 4 shows the two constructions are inverse, using the uniqueness clauses of det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf and def-weil-pbc-sheafification; the morphism compatibility is checked on sections. Edge cases pass: the empty profinite set gives the zero ring, a singleton gives an ordinary ring, noncommutative rings are excluded by the symmetry equation, and the unit on disconnected S is a(Z). No new nodes.
